prompt:
Use case: illustration-story. Asset: one 4:3 landscape painting for The Burnt Book Sanskrit learning story. Request 1536 x 1152 native output or the closest supported native 4:3 resolution. Refined Indian watercolor with restrained gouache on warm ivory paper; organic detail, quiet ochre, sage, dusty terracotta, muted indigo. Warm, gentle, evocative storytelling, consistent character design.
Canonical scene brief: The library at morning: the knotted-cord spirit holding up a book and a question mark made of rope; Dādī tapping a shelf, Śuka whispering to you; sunbeams crossing the rows of books.
Character appearances:
you: Always seen from behind or at a distance, face never detailed, so every learner can be the hero: a young person in a simple ochre kurta with a cloth shoulder bag.
dadi: A warm, sharp-eyed grandmother in her seventies, silver hair in a low bun, round spectacles, a cream cotton sari with a thin maroon border and a grey shawl; carries a cloth-bound notebook.
shuka: A bright green rose-ringed parrot with a red beak and a faint pink and black neck ring, a little scruffy, very expressive eyes; usually on your shoulder or Dādī's.
acarya: A very old, serene scholar with a white beard and a saffron shawl, a palm-leaf manuscript always under his arm, kind half-closed eyes.
ganaka: A small grey spirit made of knotted cords, with two round pebbles for eyes and a cord of beads trailing behind.
Phone-first composition: clear compact narrative grouping, essential faces, hands and objects comfortably inside all edges. Show the complete scene without border. No collage or multi-panel layout.
Owner-approved writing: render the following EXACT text, and no other writing, on the physical surface described in the scene. Use generous size, clear orthographic shapes and accurate Devanagari. The same text remains live app content. Do not substitute, omit, add or invent letters. No watermark, UI or extra labels.
? All human and humanoid figures wear complete opaque traditional clothing or robes.

title.hi: हर अलमारी के लिए एक प्रश्न

image.brief: The library at morning: the knotted-cord spirit holding up a book and a question mark made of rope; Dādī tapping a shelf, Śuka whispering to you; sunbeams crossing the rows of books.

alt.en: A knotted-cord spirit holds up a book and a rope question mark in a library
alt.hi: गाँठदार डोरियों का भूत पुस्तक और रस्सी का प्रश्नचिह्न उठाए हुए

narration.en: Ganaka stops pointing and starts asking. “Who wrote this? What is in that? Which one is lost?” He asks it of every shelf, and each time Dādī answers with the same small word, one that the shelves seem to enjoy: कः, का, किम्. Śuka whispers to you: “Same ending as ‘that’, but with a K.”
narration.hi: गणक इशारा करना छोड़कर पूछने लगता है। “यह किसने लिखा? उसमें क्या है? कौन-सा खो गया है?” वह हर अलमारी से पूछता है, और हर बार दादी एक ही छोटे शब्द से उत्तर देती हैं, जो अलमारियों को भाता है: कः, का, किम्। शुक आपके कान में फुसफुसाता है: “‘वह’ जैसे ही प्रत्यय, पर क से शुरू।”

body.en: {{किम्}} asks “who? what? which?” Its forms are the forms of {{तद्}} with {{क-}} in place of {{त-}}: {{कः}} (who, masculine), {{का}} (who, feminine), {{किम्}} (what). {{यद्}} is “who, which, that”, and goes with {{तद्}}: {{यः … सः}}, “who … he”.

title.en: तद्, किम्, यद्: side by side

caption.en: The same pronoun pattern in the masculine singular

note.en: The odd endings (coloured) are the same in all three: {{-स्मै}}, {{-स्मात्}}, {{-स्मिन्}}.

title.en: कः, का, किम् and यः, या, यत्
title.hi: कः, का, किम् और यः, या, यत्

caption.en: Who and which, first case, three genders
caption.hi: कौन और जो, प्रथमा, तीन लिंग

note.en: {{किम्}} for the neuter, {{यत्}} for the neuter; the others follow {{तद्}}.

body.en: A sentence with {{यः}} (who) is answered by {{सः}} (he): {{यः पठति सः पण्डितः}}, “who reads, he is learned”. The feminine is {{या … सा}} and the neuter {{यत् … तत्}}. The same pronoun, in any case, in both halves: {{यस्मै … तस्मै}}.
body.hi: {{यः}} (जो) वाला वाक्य {{सः}} (वह) से पूरा होता है: {{यः पठति सः पण्डितः}}, ‘जो पढ़ता है, वह विद्वान् है’। स्त्रीलिंग {{या … सा}} और नपुंसक {{यत् … तत्}}। दोनों भागों में एक ही सर्वनाम, किसी भी विभक्ति में: {{यस्मै … तस्मै}}।

meaning.en: Who reads, he is a scholar.
meaning.hi: जो पढ़ता है, वह विद्वान् है।

meaning.en: She who writes is the girl.
meaning.hi: जो लिखती है, वह कन्या है।

prompt.en: Fill in the missing forms of the table.
Fill in the missing forms of {{यद्}}.
Join each question word to its meaning.
prompt.hi: हर प्रश्नवाचक शब्द को उसके अर्थ से जोड़िए।

prompt.en: Say: “Who reads, he is a scholar.”
prompt.hi: कहिए: ‘जो पढ़ता है, वह विद्वान् है।’

explain.en: {{यः पठति सः पण्डितः}}: the pair {{यः … सः}}.

success.en: “यः पठति सः पण्डितः,” you say. Ganaka goes very still. Then, in a small dry voice, the first thing he has said in days: “कः अहम्?” “Who am I?” “गणकः,” says Dādī. “The counter.” The cords begin to tie themselves into neat rows.
success.hi: “यः पठति सः पण्डितः,” आप कहते हैं। गणक एकदम स्थिर हो जाता है। फिर छोटी सूखी आवाज़ में, कई दिनों में उसकी पहली बात: “कः अहम्?” “मैं कौन हूँ?” “गणकः,” दादी कहती हैं। “गिनने वाला।” डोरियाँ अपने-आप सुघड़ पंक्तियों में गठने लगती हैं।

failure.en: Ganaka tilts his head. The pair is {{यः … सः}}: who … he.
failure.hi: गणक सिर टेढ़ा करता है। जोड़ी है {{यः … सः}}: जो … वह।
